articles.title: Kazakhstan set to receive Russian Su-57 fighter jets within two years: Reports
articles.summary: International News: Kazakhstan is expected to receive its first Russian Su-57 fifth-generation fighter jets within the next two years, according to multiple Kazakh and Ru.
articles.body: Kazakhstan is expected to receive its first Russian Su-57 fifth-generation fighter jets within the next two years, according to multiple Kazakh and Russian reports, marking a major step in the country's air force modernisation.The reports, cited by Military Watch Magazine, indicate that Kazakhstan may have already placed orders for the Russian aircraft following confirmation in 2025 that several countries had ordered the Su-57.Kazakhstan's Air Defence Forces currently operate combat aircraft of Soviet and Russian origin, and the reported acquisition would introduce fifth-generation fighters into its fleet for the first time.The specific aircraft type has not been confirmed by most sources. However, only three fifth-generation fighters are currently available for export internationally: Russia's Su-57, China's J-35 and the US F-35.An F-35 acquisition by Kazakhstan is considered unlikely for political reasons, while China's J-35 could emerge as a potential competitor to the Russian fighter in Central Asia.China has already expanded its presence in the region's combat aircraft market. In the early 2020s, it supplied JF-17 Block 3 fighters to Azerbaijan and J-10C fighters to Uzbekistan, both replacing Soviet-era MiG-29 aircraft.Su-57 could replace Kazakhstan's Su-27The Su-57 is expected to replace Kazakhstan's ageing Su-27 fleet and could potentially replace MiG-31 aircraft at a later stage.If confirmed, the procurement would make Kazakhstan the second former Soviet republic after Russia to operate a fifth-generation fighter and potentially the second foreign customer for the Su-57 after Algeria.The Russian aircraft is generally considered less technologically advanced than the Chinese J-35 and US F-35 in several areas. However, it offers advantages including relatively lower maintenance requirements, longer range, extensive combat experience and access to a range of specialised missile systems.The reported acquisition would therefore deepen Kazakhstan's existing reliance on Russian-origin military aviation while giving its air force access to a more advanced generation of combat aircraft.

articles.title: A Colombian man struggling to build his own home helped create Lego-like bricks from recycled plastic; by 2015 the system was sheltering 42 displaced families and could build a 40-sq-m home in 5 days
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A Colombian architect has developed a construction system that turns discarded plastic and rubber into blocks for temporary and permanent homes. The b.
articles.body: A Colombian architect has developed a construction system that turns discarded plastic and rubber into blocks for temporary and permanent homes. The blocks can be assembled and dismantled like lego without glue, cement or water, offering a cheaper alternative to traditional construction in rural areas.Fernando Llanos, who had been trying to build his own house but faced difficulties transporting construction materials to his property in Cundinamarca. He eventually began exploring plastic as an alternative building material.The project was developed by Conceptos Plasticos. According to Extrusiones SA's report, the company’s system uses industrial plastic as well as plastic collected from ordinary consumers. Different types of plastic are mixed depending on the properties required for a building. The finished blocks are made through extrusion, in which the plastic is melted and poured into moulds. The blocks were designed for one and two-storey homes, with major elements such as walls and beams made from recycled plastic.Four people can build a house in five daysOne of the main features of the system is that the houses can be assembled and taken apart. In an interview with Semana Sustainable, architect Oscar Andres Mendez explained how the process works.“Four people can build a 40-square-metre house in five days and take it apart in three days. The houses are transferable, meaning they can be moved anywhere. The blocks fit together, so there is no need for glue, cement or water, just a hammer and a wrench.”The company had already used the system for temporary shelters for people displaced by violence. In 2015, it built a shelter for 42 families in Guapi, Cauca. The design was adapted for mobility and local weather conditions, with the recycled plastic blocks allowing the shelters to be dismantled and moved elsewhere within the municipality.By the time of the interview, three shelters in Guapi, each covering 400 square metres and housing 242 displaced people in total were also built. Some houses in Valle del Cauca had been purchased by private individuals, while the company had also exported its products to Costa Rica. It was also preparing to inaugurate 10 houses in Cartagena.How Plastic waste helps buildingsThe company does not use just one kind of plastic. Mendez said it works with industrial plastic and material that has passed through consumers' hands. The company buys plastic from businesses and some groups of recyclers.“Each type of plastic gives the product different properties. Some provide flexibility, while others provide rigidity, and so on. Once we have defined the design and the needs of the house we want to build, we mix several types of plastic,” Mendez said.Developing the right formula was not simple. Used plastic behaves differently from new material and required more experimentation before the blocks could be produced.Mendez said, “Working with virgin plastic is simple because there are defined parameters, but used plastic requires more experimentation.”The company holds patents for the blocks and said it was the only manufacturer of them in Colombia and abroad at the time.The blocks undergo treatment intended to make them fire-resistant. The plastic structure can also make buildings resistant to earthquakes.Designed to cost lessCost is another part of the project's appeal. The construction is 30 per cent cheaper than traditional systems in rural areas.The use of recycled material is also intended to reduce the amount of plastic sent to landfills. The project said it could lower water and energy consumption and CO2 emissions through the use of recycled materials.For Mendez, however, the project was about more than construction and waste management. He wanted recycling to be linked directly with housing.“At the moment, we have a major project in which we want to promote education further. Although we were already visiting schools and giving talks, we want citizens to realise that simply separating their waste and taking it to a nearby collection point can help provide someone with decent housing.”He described the work as one that 'closes the plastic cycle', connecting an environmental problem with a social need.Addressing concerns about plastic homesThe idea of living in a house made from waste can raise concerns about safety and health. Mendez said people often associate a plastic house with bags or a tent rather than a solid building material.“When we say, ‘this is a plastic house’, people imagine bags or something like a tent. They never think about hard materials such as soft-drink bottle caps or paint cans, which are also made of plastic.”He said people's reactions often changed after they saw the blocks and understood how the plastic was transformed.Health was another common question. Mendez said people asked whether living in houses made from waste could cause illnesses or allergies.He explained that the material goes through temperatures above 300 degrees, which it said ensures the death of microorganisms. It also worked with clean plastics that had already gone through grinding and washing before reaching the company.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1881, Judge Owen Denny shipped 60 Chinese pheasants to America because he liked their meat; the survivors helped establish a wild population in Oregon
articles.summary: US News: Judge Owen Nickerson Denny wanted Chinese pheasants in Oregon partly because he liked eating them. In 1881, while serving as the United States consul .
articles.body: Judge Owen Nickerson Denny wanted Chinese pheasants in Oregon partly because he liked eating them. In 1881, while serving as the United States consul general in Shanghai, he arranged for about 60 ring-necked pheasants to be shipped from China to Washington state. Most survived the ocean voyage, but the difficult journey from Port Townsend to Oregon killed many of them. The few that remained were released along the lower Columbia River. Denny sent more birds the following year, and the 1882 release in Oregon’s Willamette Valley became the first successful introduction of ring-necked pheasants in the United States, according to the Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife.Denny first encountered the birds in ChinaDenny was an Oregon native who had entered the diplomatic service and was serving in China when he became interested in the pheasants living around Shanghai. The birds were already being trapped by Chinese farmers and sold as food. Historical accounts record that Denny considered the birds good eating and wanted to see them established in Oregon. He eventually arranged to have them captured and transported across the Pacific along with other Chinese birds and plants. HistoryLink, a Washington historical organization, records Denny’s own explanation of the decision. He wrote that the pheasants were delicious and that he imagined what it would be like to release them in Oregon.The first shipment went badlyThe pheasants left China aboard the Otago, a ship that reached Port Townsend on March 13, 1881. Most of the birds survived the ocean crossing. The birds had to be transported from Port Townsend to Portland, and the unfamiliar movement of trains and boats caused them to panic. According to a historical account compiled by HistoryLink, the pheasants beat themselves against the bars of their cages during the journey. Only a small number survived the trip to Oregon, which were released on the lower Columbia River near Portland, but historians have disagreed about how successfully this first group established itself. Some later accounts credited the surviving birds with reproducing, while others considered the first attempt unsuccessful.The 1882 release established the Oregon populationDenny arranged another shipment in 1882, this time sending ring-necked pheasants directly toward Oregon. The birds were released in the Willamette Valley, where farmland, grain and vegetation provided suitable habitat. The Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife identifies that 1882 release as the first successful introduction of ring-necked pheasants in the United States. The birds adapted to the agricultural landscape and their numbers grew rapidly. Denny made another shipment in 1884, with additional birds released on Protection Island near Port Townsend. The pheasants continued to spread through Oregon and Washington.The birds multiplied quicklyHistoryLink records that ring-necked pheasants had spread through Oregon and Washington by the late 19th century. Oregon eventually opened its first pheasant hunting season in 1892, and reports from the period said hunters killed about 50,000 birds on the first day. The birds were initially known in Oregon as China pheasants or Denny pheasants. Their descendants spread beyond the original release sites, through the help of further introductions and transfers to other parts of the country. The Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife describes the Willamette Valley as the site of the first successful U.S. introduction and notes that the birds soon expanded into the tens of thousands.From Oregon to other statesThe success of the Pacific Northwest population encouraged people elsewhere in the United States to introduce pheasants for hunting. The ring-necked pheasant is native to Asia, not North America. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration notes that after Denny’s introduction, ring-necked pheasants were released in practically every U.S. state.Not every American pheasant population can be traced directly to Denny’s original birds, however. Later introductions involved other pheasant stocks and releases by game farms and private organizations. Still, the Oregon population became the model for establishing the species in the wild in the United States. Oregon wildlife officials describe ring-necked pheasants as farmland birds that depend heavily on cereal grains and other seeds, with taller vegetation providing cover.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A Tulsa house from ‘The Outsiders’ was falling apart; Danny Boy O’Connor turned it into a museum
articles.summary: US News: Danny Boy O’Connor first saw the Tulsa house being used as the Curtis brothers’ home in The Outsiders when he was touring the city with House of Pain .
articles.body: Danny Boy O’Connor first saw the Tulsa house being used as the Curtis brothers’ home in The Outsiders when he was touring the city with House of Pain in 2009. The 1920s bungalow at 731 North St. Louis Avenue was still standing, but it was badly deteriorated. Years later, O’Connor bought the property and decided not to repair it as a private home; he wanted to turn it into a museum devoted to S.E. Hinton’s novel and Francis Ford Coppola’s 1983 film. Smithsonian reports that O’Connor bought the house in 2015, while the museum’s own account and a 2016 fundraiser describe the purchase as taking place in 2016.The house had been left in poor conditionSmithsonian describes the one-story Craftsman bungalow as being in terrible condition when he eventually bought it. O’Connor estimated that simply making the property livable would require about $150,000. Instead of stopping at a basic renovation, he planned to restore the house to resemble its appearance in the movie and fill it with material connected to The Outsiders. The project would eventually require more time and money than he had expected.A contemporary report from Tulsa television station KJRH said O’Connor planned to reproduce the living room and dining room from the film, down to details including the couch, green curtains, fish bowl and pencil sharpeners.O’Connor had discovered the house years earlierIn 2009, while in Tulsa with House of Pain, O’Connor paid a cab driver $100 to take him around the city looking for locations from The Outsiders. He found the Curtis brothers’ house and was struck by how poorly it had been maintained. The discovery also led him to establish the Delta Bravo Urban Exploration Team, a group that documented locations associated with movies and other pieces of popular culture.O’Connor had grown up with a difficult family life and later struggled with alcohol and drugs. In the Outsiders story, he identified with the Curtis brothers and their experiences of family, hardship and loyalty. By the time the property went up for sale, O’Connor had decided that he wanted to save it. Smithsonian reported that he had little memorabilia from the movie at the time, just a poster, but still chose to turn the house into a museum.S.E. Hinton helped with the restorationBefore moving ahead with the museum, O’Connor contacted S.E. Hinton, who wrote The Outsiders while she was a teenager in Tulsa. Hinton agreed to support the project and contributed $10,000, according to Smithsonian. She also gave O’Connor a brown leather jacket worn in the film by Matt Dillon and C. Thomas Howell.The restoration was initially expected to take about six months. Instead, it stretched beyond three years and ultimately cost about $175,000, according to Smithsonian. The early fundraising effort shows how different the final project was from the original plan. A 2016 GoFundMe campaign launched by O’Connor described the property as being in extremely poor condition and sought money to restore it to its movie appearance. The campaign said the goal was to open the house to the public as a museum containing O’Connor’s collection of Outsiders memorabilia.The film set became the museum’s blueprintThe restoration was based on the 1983 movie rather than simply recreating a generic 1920s Tulsa home, and the museum’s collection eventually grew to include movie costumes, furniture, photographs, paintings, foreign editions of the book and other memorabilia. Smithsonian reported that the roughly 1,400-square-foot interior includes Ponyboy’s desk, wardrobe pieces and props associated with the film. The house itself remains recognizable from the film. The museum describes its purpose as preserving both the home and memorabilia from The Outsiders, which was filmed in Tulsa in 1982.The museum finally opened in 2019O’Connor’s six-month estimate turned into a restoration lasting more than three years, and the Outsiders House Museum officially opened in August 2019. By then, the restored house had become a public museum rather than simply a preserved movie location. Smithsonian reported that about 20,000 people visited in 2022, with school groups visiting during the week and the general public attending on weekends. The museum remains at 731 North St. Louis Avenue in Tulsa, and its current site lists weekend public hours and describes the property as dedicated to preserving the house and memorabilia from the film.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 750 dead, 20,000 deployed as rising rivers hamper rescue ops - top developments
articles.summary: South Asia News: The death toll from the catastrophic floods that struck Nepal and China's Tibet this week has risen to 750, while more than 3,000 people remain missin.
articles.body: The death toll from the catastrophic floods that struck Nepal and China's Tibet this week has risen to 750, while more than 3,000 people remain missing, as authorities warned of possible fresh flooding and rescuers continued operations in difficult conditions.The disaster was triggered by a glacier collapse on Wednesday, unleashing torrents of ice, rock, mud and debris through Himalayan river systems. The floods devastated settlements, destroyed bridges and roads, and damaged hydropower infrastructure across the affected areas.As of the latest updates on Sunday, 734 people were confirmed dead in Nepal, while 2,498 people remained missing, according to Nepal's disaster authorities.On the Chinese side in Tibet, authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, taking the combined missing toll to more than 3,000.Here are the top developments from the disaster:Fresh flood warnings issued as river levels riseNepalese authorities warned residents in flood-hit districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River on Sunday.Flood warning notices were sent to people's phones as rescue teams continued efforts to clear damaged sections of the highway linking Kathmandu with some of the worst-hit areas.The warnings came after Chinese authorities informed Nepal that water flow had increased upstream, Dharam Raj Uprety, chief executive of Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, told news agency AP.The NDRRMA also warned rescue and relief personnel in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and surrounding areas to exercise caution as the flow in the Bhote Koshi River increased further.Fresh rain also caused water levels in the Trishuli River to rise, prompting residents and rescue workers to move to higher ground, Reuters reported.Rescue focus shifts to people trapped in hydropower tunnelsRescue operations are increasingly focused on hundreds of people believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower projects after the floods swept through the region.Nepal has sought specialised international assistance for tunnel rescue operations. Foreign ministry spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said the country did not require foreign help for general rescue operations but needed support in areas including tunnel rescue, DNA testing, refrigerated storage of bodies and forensic identification.Indian and Chinese experts are assisting efforts to open tunnels.Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal told news agency ANI that more than 4,000 people had been rescued over the previous three days and that specialised teams had arrived to assist with tunnel rescue operations.According to the NDRRMA, 279 people, including 227 foreign nationals, have been rescued by helicopter from a hydropower tunnel.Over 8,000 rescued as nearly 20,000 security personnel deployedNepal's disaster authority said 8,186 people have so far been rescued.The rescue effort has involved 19,895 security personnel, including:8,399 Nepal Army personnel7,293 Nepal Police personnel4,203 Armed Police Force Nepal personnelThe NDRRMA said 2,974 people were rescued by the Nepal Army, 2,699 by Nepal Police and 2,513 by the Armed Police Force Nepal.The disaster has also left 242 people injured, while surgical medical teams have been deployed in affected areas.Nepal seeks DNA testing and forensic support to identify bodiesAuthorities are seeking specialised forensic assistance to identify the hundreds of bodies recovered from the disaster zone."We are seeking additional support for forensic laboratories. We have found more than 600 bodies, many of them in very difficult conditions to identify. We need to conduct rapid DNA analysis," foreign minister Khanal said.Unidentified bodies recovered during rescue operations have been kept across 21 hospitals in various districts, according to the NDRRMA.The latest Indian assistance includes forensic experts equipped to support DNA analysis.India sends fourth relief flight carrying 11 tonnes of suppliesIndia has sent a fourth flight to Kathmandu carrying relief supplies and specialised technical assistance for Nepal's rescue operations.External affairs minister S Jaishankar said the flight brought "essential supplies and technical capabilities" to support ongoing rescue and relief efforts.According to the Indian Embassy in Nepal, the aircraft carried 11 tonnes of relief material, including a tunnel technical team, forensic experts for DNA analysis, blankets, sleeping bags, tarpaulins, plastic sheets and hygiene kits.Foreign minister Khanal said four Indian flights carrying relief supplies had arrived in Nepal and expressed gratitude for India's assistance.More than 2,400 people missing in Nepal, including foreignersOf the 2,419 people reported missing or out of contact in an earlier NDRRMA update, 589 were foreign nationals, while 127 were Nepalis accompanying foreign tourists.The missing included 933 people linked to hydropower projects, with 562 missing in Rasuwa and 115 in Nuwakot.On the Tibetan side, authorities said 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries were among those missing, according to Reuters. They included 104 Nepalis, 49 Indians, 33 Latvians, 18 Americans and 15 Britons.New lake threat eases, but another landslide creates fresh riskRescue operations have repeatedly been disrupted by bad weather and concerns over a lake that formed across the Nepal-China border after the glacier collapse.The lake had largely drained by Saturday evening, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.However, drones later detected a landslide 2.8 km downstream of the lake, creating another dam and a fresh pool of water. Authorities moved rescue personnel near the Gyirong border crossing to safety.China and Nepal are continuing to monitor water levels and other potential hazards in the disaster zone.Infrastructure damage leaves communities cut offThe floods destroyed large concrete and suspension bridges, leaving communities on opposite sides of rivers cut off from each other.Homes and businesses that survived the initial flooding remained without electricity in some areas, with damaged power poles and wires lying in the mud.The Prithivi Highway, a key route for food, fuel and other supplies entering Kathmandu, remained operational in large parts, although some sections continued to require repairs.The Nepal government has released cash assistance, including NPR 10 million each for Rasuwa and Nuwakot, NPR 5 million for Dhading and NPR 67.5 million for 15 local municipalities.Authorities have also dispatched 37 trucks carrying food and non-food relief materials, while helicopter flights have been used to transport supplies to affected areas.International assistance continuesInternational assistance for Nepal's flood response is continuing, with India, China, the United States and Malaysia extending support.India has sent four flights carrying relief supplies and specialised technical assistance. The fourth flight carried 11 tonnes of relief material, including a tunnel technical team and forensic experts for DNA analysis.The United States has provided more than $3.6 million in humanitarian assistance, including emergency food support for up to 10,000 flood-affected households, the US Embassy in Kathmandu said on Sunday.The assistance also includes emergency supplies, while the US is coordinating with the Nepal government and humanitarian organisations on further support.Malaysia on Sunday said it would send a specialised disaster search-and-rescue team to Nepal and provide $1 million in financial aid.China has mobilised more than 2,100 rescue workers and allocated at least 220 million yuan ($32.7 million) for relief efforts.Beijing is also providing emergency aid, relief supplies, satellite and hydrological data and tunnel rescue experts to Nepal.Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi told his Nepalese counterpart that the disaster was the countries' "most severe cross-border disaster" in recent years.Nepal's LGBTQ+ community holds candlelight vigilMembers of Nepal's LGBTQ+ community gathered in Kathmandu on Saturday for a candlelight vigil to honour those killed and pray for people still missing.The event was organised by the Blue Diamond Society, which cancelled its planned Nepal Pride Parade and GaiJatra Celebration in view of the disaster."We organised this small gathering to light candles and pray for the eternal peace of all who lost their lives in this disaster, and to pray that those who are still missing are found as quickly as possible," a community member told news agency PTI.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
